criteria.description: Correctly explains lasso's constant-slope/corner-at-zero shape and why it produces exact zeros.

solutions.fullSolution: Ridge's penalty beta_j^2 has zero slope at beta_j=0: shrinking further costs less and less gradient pressure, so there's little push to reach exactly zero. Lasso's penalty |beta_j| has constant-magnitude slope everywhere except a non-differentiable corner at 0; this constant pull doesn't weaken as beta_j shrinks, so the optimum can land exactly at the corner if the loss gradient isn't enough to overcome it. Hence lasso performs feature selection (exact zeros), ridge only shrinks.

criteria.description: Correctly explains why training error is always minimized at lambda=0.
Correctly explains why cross-validation instead gives a non-degenerate criterion.

solutions.fullSolution: Any regularization term can only pull beta away from the unregularized least-squares minimizer, which by definition minimizes training error; so training error is weakly worse for any lambda>0, meaning minimizing training error over lambda always picks lambda=0. But lambda=0 is the maximal-variance, most-overfitting-prone setting. Cross-validation estimates error on held-out data, which genuinely worsens as lambda->0 (overfitting) and as lambda->infinity (underfitting), giving a real, non-degenerate criterion.

criteria.description: Correctly applies the chain rule through sigma_i to get the per-point derivative expression.
Correctly simplifies the bracket to (p_i - y_i) and assembles the full gradient.

solutions.fullSolution: Per-point: d/dbeta[y_i log p_i + (1-y_i) log(1-p_i)] = [y_i/p_i - (1-y_i)/(1-p_i)] * p_i(1-p_i) * phi(x_i). Simplify bracket*p_i(1-p_i) = y_i(1-p_i) - (1-y_i)p_i = y_i - p_i. So derivative of -[...] is (p_i-y_i)phi(x_i). Summing over i and adding 2*lambda*beta: grad L = X^T(p-y) + 2*lambda*beta. (Independently verified with SymPy.)
